title: Handle a production incident
summary: What the on-call engineer does from the first alert until the service is back and the lessons are written down: who to call, how to keep customers informed and when to escalate.

resources.title: Incident severity levels
resources.description: SEV1 to SEV4 with examples, and who must be told for each.

resources.title: Skill: draft the incident timeline
resources.description: Builds the timeline from the incident channel, the alerts and the deployments.

prerequisites.title: You are on the on-call rota
prerequisites.description: Your PagerDuty account is in the schedule of your service and the app is installed on your phone.

prerequisites.title: Alerts for your service
prerequisites.description: Without alerts nobody is paged; without a dashboard nobody sees the impact.

actors.name: You
actors.description: The on-call engineer of the service.

actors.name: Incident commander
actors.description: An SRE on duty who leads SEV1 and SEV2 incidents.

actors.name: Service desk
actors.description: Updates the status page and answers customers.

steps.title: Page the on-call engineer
steps.description: An alert fires or someone raises an incident by hand in PagerDuty.

steps.title: Acknowledge the page
instructions: Acknowledge in PagerDuty within 5 minutes.
Open the service dashboard linked in the alert.

steps.title: Decide the severity
instructions: Check how many customers are affected and which functions are down.
Pick SEV1 to SEV4 from the severity table.
Set the severity on the PagerDuty incident.

steps.title: SEV1 or SEV2?
instructions: Answer Yes when many customers are affected or a main function such as sign-in or payment is down.

steps.title: Open the incident channel and call the commander
instructions: Press 'Start incident channel' in PagerDuty; it creates #inc-<number>.
Page the incident commander from the same screen.
Post what you see and what you have tried.

steps.title: Lead the incident
steps.description: The commander runs the call, decides who does what and posts an update every 30 minutes.

steps.title: Update the status page
steps.description: The service desk publishes the first notice within 15 minutes of a SEV1 and updates it with every commander update.

steps.title: Restore the service
steps.description: Restore first, find the cause later. The quickest fix is usually rolling back the last release or turning off a feature flag.
instructions: Check the deployments of the last 24 hours in Argo CD.
If a release is the likely cause, roll it back.
Otherwise turn off the newest feature flag or scale up the service.
Post every action and its time in the incident channel.

steps.title: Service back to normal?
instructions: Answer Yes when error rate and response time are back to the level before the incident.

steps.title: Escalate to the next level
steps.description: The commander pages the secondary on-call and the team lead, and raises the severity if the impact grew.

steps.title: Resolve the incident
instructions: Watch the dashboard for 15 minutes after the fix.
Resolve the incident in PagerDuty with a one-line summary.
Ask the service desk to close the status page notice.

steps.title: Write the postmortem
steps.description: Needed for SEV1 and SEV2 within five working days. It looks for causes, not for someone to blame.
instructions: Copy the postmortem template.
Write the timeline, the impact and the causes.
Agree actions with an owner and a date for each.
Create a Jira ticket per action and link them.
